why: Rule 1 at the only deg-3 junction: 8.3cm hadron rises 58k->105k and stops at 9010, the muon arm cools away and stops at 9006 with a Michel chain, the 48cm arm is flat MIP so its 43-deg kink at 9019 into the 235k proton is a pion interaction, not the vertex.
Rule 1 clean: 4.7cm proton falls 330k->90k into 19003 (stops at 19004) and the 41cm muon cools away from 19003 to its 118k Bragg at 19002, which carries the short Michel segment 19001.
Rule 1 perfect three-prong star: all 3 segments rise away, with monotone Bragg rises to 230k at 10005 and 190k at 10001, and 10004 is the lowest-z candidate.

Single 66cm track; the 13000 end has a real multi-cm monotone rise to 180k on the proton template while the 13001 end is only one hot point (hot-blob trap), so the track cools toward 13001, which is also the lower-z end.
Rule 8: nothing but a handful of sub-cm blobs, largest cluster 1.5cm, no readable direction or junction anywhere, so any click is as good as another and I abstain.
Rule 1 at a deg-4 junction: 27.6cm proton rises monotonically to 260k at 12001 and the 187cm muon has its 220k Bragg at 12000, both pointing away, and 12005 is the lowest-z candidate.

Only readable object is the 24cm segment; its charge is concentrated at the 7000 end and it cools toward 7001, and the scattered downstream blobs sit beyond 7000, so 7001 is the upstream start (also the lower z).

Rule 3 excludes the big cluster: the 76cm track has a textbook 290k muon Bragg at 16001 with the cluster-67 Michel spray on it, entering at y=200, so the remaining structure is cluster 66, whose charge rises monotonically 28k->67k from 66018 to its stop at 66019.

Low-energy tangle; I take the hot deg-3 junction carrying the 3.4cm 77k proton stub plus a 4.3cm stub that rises away, since a proton cannot be born mid-shower, but rule 1 read literally prefers 17002 20cm away so this is close to a guess.

The 166cm near-vertical track is flat MIP with no Bragg at either end (both 5cm means are inflated by 1-2 point spikes), and everything else in the event is sub-cm dots, so there is no readable neutrino vertex and I abstain.

Rule 1 with both prongs measured: 24.3cm proton rises monotonically 100k->250k to its stop at 15004 and the 297cm muon runs forward in +z to its Bragg at 15002; 15003 is also the lowest-z candidate at z=33.7.

The 11.9cm proton rises monotonically 130k->200k away from 7002 and stops at 7003, while the 19cm and 184cm muon segments are exactly collinear through 7004 (a segmentation break) and exit flat MIP at the wall, so 7002 is the track start and lowest z.

Rule 1 at the real three-prong junction: the 8.1cm proton rises monotonically 35k->205k over 6cm and stops at 18001, the 110cm muon cools away to its Bragg at 18000, and the forward shower chain (clusters 24/58/60/61) leads off in +z from this point.

The only fitted track is a 25cm proton whose profile follows the stopping-proton template down from 330k at 21000, so it cools toward 21002, which is also the lower-z end and the upstream start of the only real object in the event.

Deg-3 junction: the 271cm prong is flat MIP running forward to the z=499 face while the 40.7cm prong stops at 1001 with a 400k tip, plus a 2.2cm third stub; confidence dropped one tier because the two long prongs leave 1002 at 167 degrees (collinearity trap).
